A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgentNet research, with readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting reliable comparison. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original MATH, APPS and BBH experiments, an evolution ablation, scaling and specialization analyses, and a task case study.

after.justification: v2 reports original MATH, BBH and API-Bank results, including additional backbones, heterogeneous-agent experiments, routing ablations and network-evolution analysis.

M1.justification: The router/executor architecture, retrieval memories, task allocation and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Removing the summation from Equation (2) aligns it with the update already present in v1's Algorithm 1, line 23; this establishes a mathematical correction rather than a new procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces APPS programming problems with API-Bank tool planning and function-calling tasks in training and evaluation. MATH and BBH remain. This changes a substantive task domain rather than merely renaming a benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPTSwarm to Table 1, including comparisons on retained MATH and BBH tasks. Figure 5 introduces a centralized Global Router and three randomized routing comparators, substantially expanding comparisons relevant to decentralized coordination. ReAct, MetaGPT and MorphAgent are retained despite inconsistent names in v1.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from GPT-4o-mini to include DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen-turbo. New protocols compare model and skill heterogeneity with three or five agents and test routing controls. API-Bank introduces randomly sampled 100-task training and test sets evaluated by accuracy. The stated MATH and BBH splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds routing-component ablations against randomized and centralized alternatives, a controlled heterogeneity study, and a three-stage network-evolution analysis. The existing warm-up ablation becomes the evolution ablation, retaining its MATH/BBH results while replacing APPS with API-Bank. The original task case study, scaling plot and specialization analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Previously reported GPT-4o-mini MATH/BBH scores remain unchanged, including AgentNet's 85.00/86.00. APPS entries disappear, while API-Bank, additional-backbone, GPTSwarm and supplementary-analysis results are added. For example, DeepSeek-V3 AgentNet reports 92.86/94.00/30.00 across MATH/BBH/API-Bank, and Figure 5 reports BBH test accuracy of 86.00 for AgentNet versus 83.00 for Global Router. These are additional comparisons, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Equation (2) removes the summation over K and the accompanying definition of K, correcting the weight-update expression to agree with the existing pseudocode. Other mathematical definitions and equations are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims concerning decentralized coordination, evolving topology, retrieval-based specialization, scalability, fault tolerance and privacy. Additional experiments do not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations attributing heterogeneous-team performance to coordination overhead versus complementary reasoning, distinguishing operation selection from agent selection, and linking evolving connections to specialization. It removes the APPS-specific explanation of MorphAgent's compilation failures. The existing limitations concerning heterogeneous environments and large-scale routing remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents API-Bank sampling, GPT-4o-mini annotation into seven task categories, and three difficulty levels. Table 1 newly specifies three agents for every multi-agent comparator; v1 did not establish that uniform setting. Generation parameters and the embedding model remain unchanged, with no added code release, hardware specification or training-time information.

R1.justification: The API-Bank citation replaces the APPS citation. GPTSwarm gains an experimental-baseline description but was already discussed and cited in v1. MetaGPT and AutoGen bibliographic updates concern the same works; the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in experimental descriptions and results discussion, with new analysis subsections, warm-up/evolution terminology changes, and promotion of limitations to a standalone section. Funding acknowledgements and an ethics statement are added, including duplicated acknowledgement headings. The core exposition and overall narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially restructured into three backbone blocks. v2 adds the heterogeneity table, routing-performance chart and network-evolution visualization, and reformats the evolution-ablation table beside its discussion. Existing case-study, scaling and specialization displays are retained and relocated rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The new routing controls directly examine a central mechanism that v1's warm-up ablation did not isolate, while heterogeneity experiments reveal a team-size-dependent limitation. Additional backbones and GPTSwarm strengthen comparative evidence, and Equation (2) becomes consistent with the algorithm. These gains are tempered by lost APPS coverage, insufficient detail about heterogeneous-agent construction, and continued reporting weaknesses: no uncertainty estimates and conflicting GPT-4o-mini API-Bank accuracies of 29.00 in Table 1 and 32.00 in Table 3. The revision provides a limited net quality improvement.
